obligation: G035 -- shared basis plus per-layer coefficients vs independent, matched bits
method: Randomized-SVD range finder; only the leading subspace is compared, an exact SVD of a 17408x10240 matrix is neither affordable nor needed. Independent gives each layer its own rank-r factorization; shared computes one column basis from the two layers concatenated and projects both onto it. The shared basis IS the alignment and it is inside the parameter budget, so there is no separate alignment cost to omit.
matched_budget: Shared rank is the largest whose parameters fit the independent budget, so sharing spends its saving on rank rather than on a smaller artifact.
error_space: FUNCTION space on the thick v2 capture, not weight cosine -- weight space already inverted a ranking once in this campaign (G033).
control: A far-apart layer pair. If sharing helps adjacent layers it should help distant ones measurably less; equal help would mean the effect is the factorization, not layer affinity.

delta_coding.method: store L_a at q4 and L_b as (L_b - dequant(L_a)) at q2, so the PAIR costs 6.5 bits/elem exactly as independent q3+q3 does
delta_coding.verdict: REFUTED, and not marginally: roughly 2x the error of independent q3+q3 at identical total bits on all three pairs and in BOTH directions. The delta carries L_a's quantization error on top of the genuine layer difference, so it has a WIDER spread than the tensor it replaces and quantizes worse at q2 than the tensor does at q3. The far pair behaves like the adjacent pair, so proximity does not help.

shared_row_basis.method: stack the pair along the OUTPUT axis and share the row space, matched parameters with the shared rank raised to spend the saving
shared_row_basis.verdict: WINS, unlike the column basis. Adjacent gate_proj L30/L31: 0.57592 against independent 0.61465, a 6.3% error reduction at slightly FEWER bits. Far pair L15/L47: 0.69274 against 0.69775, only 0.7%. THE ADJACENCY SIGNATURE THE COLUMN BASIS FAILED TO SHOW IS PRESENT HERE -- adjacent benefits 9x more than distant, which is what the spectral observation that opened this obligation predicted.

corrected_verdict: AXIS-DEPENDENT, which the original refutation did not distinguish. Sharing the COLUMN space (the contraction axis) LOSES on 3/3 pairs. Sharing the ROW space (the output axis) WINS, and wins 9x more for adjacent layers than distant ones. The blanket 'REFUTED AT MATCHED BITS' was drawn from the column basis alone and is too broad.
what_still_limits_it: The row-basis win is measured at ~1.03 bits/elem where the pair errors are 0.58-0.70, deep in the DEAD zone against the coherent anchor's 0.198. It is a 6.3% improvement to something unusable. G034 separately measured low-rank at a usable 3.25 bits/elem running 2.93x worse than flat q3, so the family's ceiling is low whichever axis is shared. Whether the row-basis advantage survives at usable fidelity is UNTESTED.
still_untested: learned orthogonal alignment applied BEFORE sharing
